title: RoboReason: Boosting Robotics-Relevant VLM Reasoning Through Scalable Data Generation
abstract: arXiv:2610.33778v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated impressive performance when integrated into robot manipulation pipelines, but real-world evaluation of VLM capabilities on downstream robotics tasks is both difficult and expensive to scale. We propose that spatial and temporal ordering tasks using images from stereo and wrist cameras attached to real-world robots are particularly well-suited for evaluating visual reasoning capabilities, as they assess skills directly applicable to robots. We evaluate VLM reasoning abilities on three questions: ordering shuffled frames conditioned on a language description of the task, ordering objects depthwise based on distance from the camera, and ordering objects from left-to-right in pixel coordinates. The complexity of these tasks can also be modulated by changing the size of the set to sort. Our experiments show that several state-of-the-art vision-language models struggle on ordering tasks. To fix

translated_title: RoboReason：通过可扩展数据生成提升机器人相关的视觉语言模型推理能力
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型（VLMs）在集成到机器人操作流水线中时展现出了令人印象深刻的性能，但在下游机器人任务上对VLM能力进行真实世界评估既困难又难以规模化。我们提出，使用安装在真实世界机器人上的立体相机和腕部相机所拍摄的图像进行空间和时间排序任务，特别适合评估视觉推理能力，因为这些任务考察的是可直接应用于机器人的技能。我们在三个问题上评估了VLM的推理能力：根据任务的语言描述对打乱的帧进行排序、基于与相机的距离对物体进行深度方向排序，以及在像素坐标中从左到右对物体进行排序。这些任务的复杂性还可以通过改变待排序集合的大小来调节。我们的实验表明，多个最先进的视觉语言模型在排序任务上表现不佳。为了解决这一问题……
tldr: 该论文提出利用真实机器人立体相机和腕部相机图像的空间与时间排序任务来评估视觉语言模型的视觉推理能力，发现当前最先进的VLM在排序任务上表现不佳，并通过可扩展的数据生成方法提升机器人相关的VLM推理能力。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes using spatial and temporal ordering tasks based on real-robot stereo and wrist camera images to evaluate visual reasoning in VLMs, shows that state-of-the-art VLMs struggle on these tasks, and boosts robotics-relevant VLM reasoning through scalable data generation.
